title: Haiti Gang Suppression Force authorisation lapses — resolution 2793's twelve-month mandate hits its hard deadline, a diary line on the Council's last day of the French presidency
source: EST: onu.diplomatie.gouv.fr/en/french-presidency-security-council-program-work, re-fetched direct 2026-09-15 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200), independently of the proposal that discovered it and reading the WHOLE 30 September line rather than the Haiti fragment. The French presidency's 'Provisional Agenda of Work of the Security Council - September 2026' ('as of' 31 August 2026, published 2 September 2026) gives Wednesday 30 September in full as: 'S-G luncheon. Wrap-up session (p.m.). Iraq/Kuwait progress update due. UNOWAS strategic review due. PSC Framework report due. Haiti GSF mandate expires.' Corroborated by securitycouncilreport.org/un-documents/haiti/ (read direct 2026-09-15, HTTP 200), whose index records 'S/RES/2793 (30 September 2025)' authorising the transition of the MSS mission into a Gang Suppression Force 'for an initial period of 12 months', vote 12 in favour with 3 abstentions - twelve months from 2025-09-30 is 2026-09-30. Corroborated independently by securitycouncilreport.org's September-2026 Haiti forecast ('The GSF was first authorised for an initial period of 12 months on 30 September 2025') and by aljazeera.com's 2026-09-04 report ('set to expire on September 30'). Estimate rather than confirmed on a schema ground that cannot be cleared here: CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs carries no UN or diplomatic slot, and the programme naming the day is captioned provisional. Resolution 2793's own operative text was NOT fetched - main.un.org/securitycouncil/en/content/sres27932025 returned an empty body on 2026-09-15 and is recorded in the ledger's probe-ref.blocked rather than substituted. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-15 by this event's own never-assessed initial research (docs/research/events/unsc-haiti-gsf-mandate-expiry-2026-09-30.md), after reading the one proposal that named this id - proposals/unsc-haiti-gsf-mandate-expiry-2026-09-30.from-unsc-haiti-gsf-mandate-adoption-2026-09-29.json, now shadowed and inert. Nothing in the proposal was contradicted; three of its open reads are advanced. THIS IS A DIARY LINE, NOT A MEETING. The primary's 30 September entry is a luncheon, a wrap-up session and four documents 'due', of which this is one; the Council has NO Haiti item scheduled on the date, and 09-30 is the last day of the French presidency. The decision belongs to the sibling adoption on 09-29. THE LAPSE PATH IS A TECHNICAL ROLLOVER, NOT A LAPSE, and this is the finding a deadline entry adds to the vote entry's nine-for-nine pass rate. Security Council Report's own study defines the device - an unaltered mandate extended by a concise resolution for a shorter period than is customary, first purpose to buy time when negotiations have reached an impasse - and three dated instances sit inside eighteen months: South Sudan/UNMISS 9 days (2025-04-30), Afghanistan/UNAMA 3 months (2026-03), and Sudan sanctions res 2828, adopted UNANIMOUSLY on 2026-09-11, four days before this assessment, rolling the measures to 2026-10-09 and the Panel of Experts to 2026-11-09. The same SCR study names exactly ONE mandate ever lost to a missed deadline: UNOMIG, terminated after Russia vetoed its rollover on 2009-06-15. A lapse here therefore needs a veto on a two-paragraph extension, and no veto has ever been cast on a Haiti text (res 2793 went 12-0-3, abstention being the objection mechanism on this file). WHY low AND symbols [] REMAIN HONEST, and why this date is less readable than the vote rather than more: the only listed company with a named Haitian asset is Royal Caribbean (Labadee), which has already cancelled every 2026 call there, so the structural channel is zero by the issuer's own decision. Measured across the SIX cruise-print-clean Haiti mandate DEADLINES since 2023 (eight dated deadlines less the two within two trading sessions of a cruise 8-K Item 2.02 print - 2024-10-02 and 2026-02-02), SPY moves 0.31% median absolute against a 0.57% baseline (0.71x its own +/-10-session regime, 1.04% max) and RCL 0.82% against 1.52% (0.54x, 1.29% max); CCL 1.46% vs 1.86%, NCLH 1.46% vs 1.87%, XLY 0.75% vs 0.87%, CL=F 1.69% vs 1.51%. THE CONTAMINATION FINDING IS THIS DOCUMENT'S OWN: the two prior security-mandate deadlines in this lineage (res 2751's on 2024-10-02, res 2793's on 2025-10-02) were quarter-START days and were extraordinarily quiet (SPY 0.08% median absolute, 0.18x local, n=2). Res 2793's twelve-month term moved the 2026 deadline onto the LAST SESSION OF Q3, where SPY runs 1.20x its own local regime (2022+, n=18; September-only, n=6, also 1.20x) and TWO of the last six September quarter-end closes (-1.22% in 2021, -1.55% in 2022) cleared 1.04%, the entire Haiti-deadline sample's maximum. In roughly one year out of three the day's ordinary quarter-end churn is larger than anything this event class has ever produced - before PCE is added. THE CORRIDOR IS THE POINT: 56 tracked events sit within +/-5 days and SEVENTEEN share 09-30 itself, including pce-2026-09-30 (confirmed, high), government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30 (estimate, high), gdp-q2-2026-third, adp-employment, chicago-pmi, dallas-fed-trimmed-mean, and three separate quarter-end index mechanics (bloomberg-agg-index-rebalance, russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective, sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight). Four adjacents are confirmed AND high: pce-2026-09-30, ism-manufacturing-2026-10-01, jobs-2026-10-02, ism-services-2026-10-05, with opec-plus-meeting-2026-10-04 the one that actually touches the nearest instruments, through fuel. A CORRECTION TO THE SIBLING'S READ FLAG: deadline dates collide with cruise prints only 2 of 8 (against 3 of 9 adoption dates), so the deadline class is the safer sample - but CCL's Q3 print cadence is 29, 30 and 29 days after its 31-August quarter end (2023-09-29, 2024-09-30, 2025-09-29), and the aggregator estimate of 2026-10-05 would be 35 days, the longest in the series; 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-30 both sit inside the observed cadence, so 'this instance looks clean' is a live question, registered as a forward test rather than asserted. SUBSTANCE, which argues for renewal: the Haiti Panel of Experts' final report, discussed by the 2653 Committee on 2026-09-03 (press.un.org SC/16452), found that operations since December 2025 halted gang expansion and cleared some areas but that the majority of Port-au-Prince remained under gang control, against a GSF standing at 1,083 military and 16 civilian personnel as of 2026-07-08 versus an authorised 5,500 uniformed plus 50 civilian - about 20% deployed, eleven months into a twelve-month mandate.
